meta.title: Two Editors, One EEPROM
meta.subtitle: Virtual players are separate processes sharing one preferences store — and roles are the strapping pins that free them

views.label: What a virtual player is
views.note: A folder of symlinks back to your assets, launched as a genuinely separate editor process.

views.label: The pref they all read
views.note: One key, scoped by product name, not by instance. Every process reads the same value.

views.label: Roles override the pref
views.note: With the dedicated server package installed, a per-player role is consulted first and the shared key is ignored.

views.label: What actually gets built
views.note: The play type decides which worlds exist. Two servers means two binds on one port.

boundaries.label: separate processes · shared library folder · no shared memory, no shared statics

cards.title: A virtual player is not a sandbox
items: It is a real second editor process with its own worlds, sockets and domain
Its folder holds symlinks to your assets and project settings, so edits appear instantly
Its own library holds only per-instance editor state; the compiled assemblies come from yours
It shares nothing at runtime: no static state crosses between processes

cards.title: The crash, and why the obvious fix fails
items: The play type preference key is scoped by product name, not by instance
Its default is client and server, so a second player builds a server world too
Two servers bind the same port; the bind failure then cascades into loader and entity errors
Changing it in play mode tools cannot help, because a virtual player has no such window

cards.title: Roles are the strapping pins
items: Installing the dedicated server package defines the roles symbol as a version define
The preference getter then asks the roles manager first and never reaches the shared key
Each player carries its own role, saved in the play mode system data file
Visible confirmation: the play type control in play mode tools goes grey

cards.title: The reading that means it worked
items: Main editor on client and server, second player on client only
Exactly one server world across every instance
Four ghosts for two players, because each player is a controller plus a capsule
A thin client is a different amputation again, and it will not load the client subscenes
